Application Areas: Anaerobic Microbial Metabolism and Carbon Cycling
Key Research Thinking Patterns: High-Resolution Structural Elucidation of Anaerobic Enzymes: Utilizing synchrotron X-ray crystallography and specialized anaerobic purification to resolve atomic-level mechanisms of metabolic enzymes, such as determining the 1.78 Å structure of SaHcd1 to understand benzoate degradation pathways.

Integrative Systems Biology of Transcriptional Control: Combining in vivo genetic assays (e.g., B1H, EMSA) with in vitro biochemical characterization to map phosphorylation-dependent DNA binding modes and regulatory networks in response regulators and RNA polymerase assembly.

Multi-Omics Driven Metabolic Pathway Mapping: Correlating shotgun proteomics, 13C-isotope tracing, and enzyme kinetics to identify functional roles of iron-sulfur clusters and map reversible enzymatic conduits for reverse electron transfer in syntrophic metabolism.

Mechanistic Dissection of Enzyme Catalysis via Site-Directed Mutagenesis: Employing QuikChange mutagenesis and steady-state kinetics (Vmax, Km) to define substrate activation mechanisms and NAD(P)+ binding motifs in short-chain dehydrogenase/reductase families.
Summary Description: Elizabeth Karr is a structural biologist specializing in the mechanistic underpinnings of anaerobic syntrophy and transcriptional regulation. She integrates high-resolution synchrotron X-ray crystallography with advanced proteomics and genetic analysis to characterize metabolic enzymes and regulatory proteins in model organisms like Syntrophus aciditrophicus and archaea. Her work resolves atomic structures of key enzymes, such as SaHcd1, elucidating their roles in fatty-acid metabolism and carbon cycling. By combining structural data with in vivo functional assays, Karr provides critical insights into bioenergetic constraints and regulatory networks, advancing our understanding of microbial ecology and potential applications in bioenergy production.
